chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no sa'y (running/walking between the hills) required for the traveler, but he should hasten a little."

key_terms.الرَّاكِبِ: The traveler (one riding an animal or vehicle)
key_terms.سَعْيٌ: Sa'y (the ritual walking/running between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.لِيُسْرِعْ: To hasten (to move quickly, indicating a shortened ritual)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Sa'y for a traveler during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the concession (*rukhsah*) for travelers regarding Sa'y, distinguishing between the obligatory full circuit for residents and the abbreviated 'hastening' (*yusr*) for those on a journey. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of easing religious duties for travelers, aligning with the Prophetic tradition where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) himself performed a shortened Sa'y when returning from Mecca. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh, ensuring that the spiritual essence of the ritual is maintained without imposing undue hardship.
